---
title: "Time Series Forecasting: Where to Start"
date: 2026-06-15
categories: [time series, forecasting]
description: "The handful of ideas that make most forecasting methods click."
---

Most time series methods, from ARIMA to gradient-boosted trees, are trying to separate a
series into a few recurring pieces:

1. **Trend** — the long-run direction.
2. **Seasonality** — patterns that repeat at fixed intervals (weekly, yearly).
3. **Noise** — what's left after trend and seasonality are accounted for.

Once a series is decomposed this way, forecasting becomes a question of which piece is
hardest to predict for your data — and that's usually what determines whether a simple
model (like exponential smoothing) will do, or whether you need something that can learn
nonlinear structure (like an ML model with engineered lag features).
